title: Lemon & Herb Roast Chicken
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Halve one lemon and push it into the cavity with the thyme and the garlic bulb, cut across the middle.
Rub the skin with oil, the juice of the second lemon, salt and plenty of pepper.
Roast for 70 minutes, basting once at the halfway mark.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving — this is not optional.

title: Overnight Oats with Berries
instructions: Stir the oats, milk, yoghurt, honey and salt together in a jar.
Seal and refrigerate overnight.
Top with berries in the morning.

title: Slow-Cooked Beef Short Rib
instructions: Heat the oven to 140°C fan.
Brown the ribs hard on every side in a casserole, then set aside.
Soften the chopped onions and carrots, stir in the tomato purée and cook for two minutes.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then return the ribs with the stock and bay.
Cover and cook for four hours, until the meat gives way to a spoon.
Skim the fat and reduce the sauce if it needs tightening.

title: Miso Glazed Aubergine
instructions: Halve the aubergines and score the flesh in a diamond pattern.
Brush with oil and roast at 200°C for 20 minutes, cut side up.
Whisk the miso, mirin, sake and sugar into a glaze.
Spoon it over the aubergines and grill for 5 minutes until blistered.
Finish with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

title: Chocolate Brownies
instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C fan and line a 20 cm tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together, then cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale and thick — this is what gives the papery top.
Fold in the chocolate, then the sifted flour, cocoa and salt.
Bake 25 minutes. The middle should still wobble.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting.

title: Apple & Blackberry Crumble
instructions: Peel and chop the apples, stew with a splash of water and half the sugar for 10 minutes.
Stir in the blackberries and tip into a baking dish.
Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs, then stir in the oats, remaining sugar and cinnamon.
Scatter over the fruit without pressing it down.
Bake at 180°C fan for 35 minutes until the top is deep gold.

title: Weeknight Carbonara
instructions: Boil the pasta in well-salted water.
Render the guanciale slowly in a cold pan until crisp.
Beat the yolks, egg and cheese with a great deal of black pepper.
Drain the pasta, keeping a mugful of water, and toss it into the pork off the heat.
Add the egg mixture and loosen with pasta water, stirring hard. The pan must not be hot enough to scramble it.

title: Green Thai Curry
instructions: Fry the paste in the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk until it splits and smells sweet.
Add the chicken and colour it in the paste.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk with the chopped aubergine and simmer 20 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar and lime until it tastes balanced.
Stir through the basil off the heat.

title: Sourdough Focaccia
instructions: Mix the flour and water and rest for an hour.
Add the starter and salt, then do four sets of stretch and folds over two hours.
Refrigerate overnight — up to 18 hours.
Tip into a well-oiled tray, dimple all over with your fingers and prove until puffy.
Scatter with rosemary and flaky salt and bake at 230°C for 22 minutes.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Soften the sliced onion and peppers in oil for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and spices and cook for one minute.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer until thick, about 15 minutes.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook until the whites set.
Crumble over feta and parsley.

title: Roasted Tomato Soup
instructions: Halve the tomatoes and roast with the quartered onions, garlic cloves and oil at 200°C for 40 minutes.
Tip everything into a pan with the stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth, adding basil at the end.
Season hard — roasted tomatoes take more salt than you expect.

title: Beef Chilli
instructions: Brown the mince in batches so it fries rather than steams.
Soften the onions, add the spices and chipotle, and return the beef.
Add the tomatoes and simmer, uncovered, for an hour.
Stir in the drained beans and the chocolate and cook 20 minutes more.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Mushroom Risotto
instructions: Fry the mushrooms hard in a dry pan, then in butter. Set aside.
Soften the finely chopped onion, add the rice and toast for two minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it disappear.
Add stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 18 minutes.
Beat in the butter, parmesan and mushrooms off the heat and rest two minutes.

title: Fish Tacos with Lime Slaw
instructions: Toss the fish in chipotle, salt and oil and fry two minutes a side.
Shred the cabbage and dress with lime juice and salt.
Warm the tortillas directly over a flame.
Build with fish, slaw, soured cream and coriander.

title: Banana Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan and line a loaf tin.
Cream the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Mash the bananas and fold them through.
Fold in the flour, bicarb and walnuts.
Bake for 55 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

title: Chickpea & Spinach Curry
instructions: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger until soft and golden.
Add the curry powder and cook until fragrant.
Tip in the chickpeas and coconut milk and simmer 15 minutes.
Wilt the spinach through at the end and season with salt and lemon.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
instructions: Soak the chopped dates in the boiling water with the bicarb for 10 minutes.
Cream the butter and half the sugar, beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour and dates with their liquid.
Bake at 170°C fan for 35 minutes.
Simmer the cream with the remaining sugar to make the toffee sauce.
Prick the sponge all over and pour half the sauce on while hot.

title: Pulled Pork Shoulder
instructions: Rub the pork all over with the mixed spices, sugar and salt. Leave overnight if you can.
Roast at 220°C for 30 minutes, then drop to 130°C.
Add the vinegar to the tray, cover tightly with foil and cook for seven hours.
Rest for 30 minutes, then pull apart with two forks.
Toss the meat through the skimmed pan juices.

title: Caesar Salad
instructions: Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste.
Whisk in the yolk, mustard and lemon, then trickle in oil until thick.
Stir through most of the grated parmesan.
Toss with torn lettuce and croutons and finish with the rest of the cheese.

title: Pad Thai
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water until pliable but not soft.
Mix the tamarind, fish sauce and sugar into a sauce.
Fry the prawns hard, push aside, scramble the eggs in the same pan.
Add the drained noodles and sauce and toss over high heat for two minutes.
Throw in beansprouts at the last moment and serve with peanuts and lime.

title: Lamb Tagine
instructions: Brown the diced lamb in batches.
Soften the onions, add the spices and cook until fragrant.
Return the lamb with the tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add the apricots for the last 30 minutes.
Scatter with toasted almonds and coriander.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
instructions: Whisk the dry ingredients in one bowl and the wet in another.
Combine with as few strokes as possible — lumps are correct.
Rest the batter 10 minutes.
Cook in a buttered pan over medium heat until bubbles set at the edges, then flip.

title: Ramen Broth from Scratch
instructions: Blanch the bones for 10 minutes, then rinse away every trace of scum.
Cover with fresh water and boil hard for 10 hours, topping up as it reduces.
Add the aromatics for the final two hours.
Strain through a fine sieve. It should be opaque and cling to a spoon.
Season with tare, not salt, when you build the bowl.

title: Halloumi & Watermelon Salad
instructions: Slice the halloumi and fry until deeply golden on both sides.
Cube the watermelon and scatter on a platter.
Lay the hot cheese over the cold melon.
Dress with lime, oil, torn mint and pepper. No salt — the cheese has plenty.

title: Beef Wellington
instructions: Sear the seasoned fillet on all sides and brush with mustard while hot. Cool completely.
Blitz the mushrooms and fry until every drop of water has gone — this takes longer than you think.
Lay out the prosciutto on cling film, spread with the duxelles, and roll the beef up tightly. Chill 30 minutes.
Wrap in pastry, seal, glaze with yolk and score.
Bake at 200°C for 35 minutes for medium rare, then rest 15 minutes.

title: Garlic Butter Prawns
instructions: Melt the butter with the sliced garlic and chilli over gentle heat until it just turns golden.
Raise the heat and add the prawns in one layer.
Turn them after 90 seconds — they are done the moment they curl.
Off the heat, add lemon and parsley and serve with bread for the butter.
